A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TARS study and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Inspection of all 12 pages of v1 and 15 pages of v2 supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original reasoning-benchmark results, training and reward ablations, LibriSpeech WER, and layer-wise analyses in Tables 1–2 and Figures 2–3.

after.justification: v2 retains these experiments and adds text-only GRPO, Qwen reward ablations, generalization evaluations, domain-level results, efficiency measurements, and qualitative cases.

M1.justification: The joint speech/text GRPO-DAPO procedure, representation and behavior rewards, correct-text reference selection and fallback, and modality-specific normalization remain unchanged. v2 clarifies mean pooling and evaluates reward variants without changing the proposed TARS algorithm.

E1.justification: Section 5.5 and Table 4 add SD-QA, covering real spoken questions with diverse accents and open-ended answers, and the WANG et al. MMSU benchmark for paralinguistic perception. The latter is explicitly distinct from the VoiceBench MMSU used in both versions. Existing training and evaluation coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same comparators, but v2 adds Text-only GRPO to the Phi-4-MM comparison in Table 2. Table 3 additionally reports CoT, standard GRPO, and individual reward-component comparisons on Qwen, which v1 did not report for that backbone. SoundMind-RL is discussed but not evaluated.

E3.justification: v2 adds a text-only optimization control, free-generation reward tracking, and an explicit runtime/memory comparison on 8 H200 GPUs over three epochs, separating offline data-generation costs. Existing main experiments retain their reported sample counts, balanced eight-completion groups, decoding procedures, and hyperparameters. Identifying the auxiliary_train split clarifies the existing data source rather than establishing a changed split.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained Phi reward ablations and layer analyses, v2 adds Qwen reward ablations, the text-only control, real-speech/paralinguistic generalization tests, a 12-domain breakdown, free-generation reward curves, efficiency analysis, and successful and persistent-error case studies. These substantially expand tests of mechanism, applicability, and failure conditions.

E5.justification: Both versions report 95% confidence intervals for layer-wise similarity, in v1 Figure 3 and v2 Figure 2. The averaging and confidence-interval description moves to Appendix E. v2 introduces no documented seed counts, repeated-run procedures, accuracy uncertainty estimates, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 and all pre-existing Table 2 values are unchanged. Added results include Text-only GRPO's 76.86% average audio and 83.76% text accuracy, Qwen behavior-only alignment reaching 77.71% versus 76.84% with both rewards, and TARS audio results of 57.40% on the new MMSU benchmark and 41.95% on SD-QA. Domain, efficiency, fallback-frequency, and qualitative findings are also added.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7 retain the same MRR definition, rewards, mean pooling, and modality-specific advantages. v2 adds explanatory prose but no new mathematical assumptions, formal results, proofs, or substantive derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same central claims: architecture-preserving on-policy trajectory alignment using two complementary rewards, narrowing the modality reasoning gap, and state-of-the-art performance among 7B-scale models on MMSU and OBQA.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 interprets the Qwen ablation as stage-dependent over-regularization, qualifying the benefit of combining rewards. New discussion addresses preservation of text reasoning, transfer to real speech and paralinguistic tasks, and persistent semantic, domain-logic, and chronological errors. The scale limitation also explicitly expands to untested smaller models.

D1.justification: v2 adds a repository pointer, identifies the MMLU auxiliary_train split, clarifies how the internal 7B Phi model relates to the official 5.6B architecture, and documents additional resource measurements. Existing LoRA hyperparameters and prompt templates are retained as Tables 5–6; relocated baseline and teacher-forcing descriptions are not new implementation details.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds discussion of manifold mixup, contrastive learning, joint speech-text training, and interleaving, and distinguishes TARS from SoundMind-RL's sparse rewards. New benchmark and distillation references are included, while the central research positioning remains. Updated author or publication information for AlignChat, Kimi-Audio, and DeepSeek-R1 concerns retained works.

P1.justification: Editing concentrates on related work, reward explanations, and a condensed experimental setup. Existing analyses are regrouped and reordered under Section 5, baseline and teacher-forcing details move to appendices, and appendix headings are reorganized. Much of the introduction, original results discussion, and conclusion remains unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds six tables, Tables 3–4 and 7–10, a training-reward plot in Figure 4, and a row in Table 2. Existing layer plots are relocated and exchange figure numbers without changed data. The hyperparameter and prompt tables become Tables 5–6, with the prompt table reformatted into one column. These substantially expand and reorganize the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v1's validation centered on two multiple-choice benchmarks and Phi reward ablations. v2 adds an important text-only GRPO control, tests real/open-ended speech and paralinguistic perception, and reveals that combined rewards are not optimal for Qwen. These additions substantially strengthen evaluation of attribution and applicability, while efficiency measurements and failure cases improve scrutiny. Some added benchmark protocols remain briefly specified and accuracy uncertainty is still unreported, but the overall validation gains are substantial.
